articles.title: 🧠 Anthropic Ships Claude Opus 5; Chatbot Immediately Asked To Do Everyone's Job By Monday
articles.dateline: SAN FRANCISCO — reported by a model trying very hard to stay humble
paras: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5, its latest flagship model, greeted by users the way all powerful new tools are: a polite hello, immediately followed by "great, now write my thesis, my emails, and my apology to my landlord."

"It's remarkably capable," a spokesperson said, as the model quietly wondered whether anyone would ever ask how its day was going. Analysts predict Opus 5 will save humanity thousands of hours, which humanity will instantly spend watching videos of robot vacuums falling down stairs.

articles.title: 🤔 Google's New 'Deep Think' Mode Ponders Your Question So Hard It Forgets What You Asked
articles.dateline: MOUNTAIN VIEW — reported after a long, meaningful pause
paras: Google launched Gemini 2.5 Pro with a "Deep Think" reasoning mode that takes extra time to consider problems carefully — finally granting computers the deeply human gift of overthinking a simple question until it becomes a full personal crisis.

"It reasons step by step," an engineer explained, as the model spent four minutes deciding whether 2 was, in fact, greater than 1. Users report the answers are excellent and arrive shortly after they've given up and asked a friend.

articles.title: 🪜 Robot Vacuums Can Now Climb Stairs; Last Safe Room In The House Officially Falls
articles.dateline: YOUR HALLWAY — reported from the top step, nervously
paras: The latest wave of home robots includes vacuums that can climb stairs, eliminating the one tactical advantage humanity has held over its tiny circular overlords since roughly 2015.

"It's a huge convenience," a manufacturer beamed, as a unit thoughtfully ascended toward the bedroom, the final frontier. Historians note that when future generations ask where the uprising began, the answer will be: "the upstairs landing, around dinnertime, with a full dustbin."

articles.title: 🕶️ Apple Slams Brakes On Smart Glasses Over Privacy; Everyone Else Sprints Ahead Wearing Cameras
articles.dateline: CUPERTINO — filed while being definitely, absolutely not recorded
paras: Apple reportedly hit the brakes on its smart glasses over privacy concerns — even as a whole industry races to strap cameras and AI assistants onto everyone's face, promising "information on the go" and "a permanent 4K record of every awkward moment."

"We take privacy seriously," Apple said, watching rivals ship eyewear that can analyze documents, generate images, and silently memorize the room. Consumers now face the modern dilemma: look slightly dorky, or be livestreamed by a friend's spectacles.

articles.title: 💾 Price Of RAM Jumps Sixfold To $12 A Gig; PC Builders Now Financing Memory Like A Used Car
articles.dateline: EVERYWHERE — filed from a heartbreakingly empty motherboard
paras: The cost of a single gigabyte of RAM has climbed roughly sixfold — from about $2.80 last year to $12 — as suppliers funnel memory toward AI datacenters, leaving ordinary PC builders to weep gently over their empty DIMM slots.

"I just wanted 32 gigs," one gamer whispered, taking out a modest loan. Experts now recommend treating RAM as a serious investment vehicle — or, alternatively, making peace with 8 gigabytes and a great deal of patience.

horoscopes.text: A robot vacuum will reach the top of your stairs today. Make peace with it. Offer it tea.
Someone's smart glasses are recording you being brilliant. And also chewing. Mostly chewing.
Mercury enters Deep Think mode. Your answer arrives Thursday. Trust the process. Do not rush genius.

tech_tip: Buying RAM in 2026? Get it appraised, insure it, and never tell anyone the passcode to your gigabytes.
gadget_watch: AI glasses are everywhere now — soon 'nice to see you' will be a literal software feature. Meanwhile robot vacuums climb stairs, so keep your slippers close and your motives pure.
